title: DISPATCH
universal_lens: The mathematical unification of these primitives rests on the isomorphism between Bayesian posterior regularization (Beta-Binomial) and copula-induced tail dependence structures. By mapping the Cornish-Fisher expansion to C-Vine simulations, we establish a rigorous bridge between local drawdown ruin probabilities and global multivariate extreme event clustering.
gsi_mapping: GSI inference utilizes Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR) over Negative Binomial count props to generate predictive intervals with finite-sample coverage guarantees. The CV penalty kappa acts as a dynamic conformal calibration parameter, ensuring that epistemic uncertainty strictly bounds the Wilson score lower confidence bound.
gse_mapping: GSE situational reasoning maps the Browne drawdown ruin condition directly to state-transition fail-closed gates. When live feed telemetry triggers negative control blocking, the engine transitions to an ABSTAIN state, enforcing Law 9 by mathematically decoupling the system from high-entropy, unverified market microstructures.

primitives.name: Bayesian Robust Kelly Engine
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Bayesian Robust Kelly engine (Beta-Binomial, Cornish-Fisher, CV penalty kappa, Browne drawdown ruin).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: f^*: optimal fraction (dimensionless), p: win probability (dimensionless), q: loss probability (dimensionless), \kappa: CV penalty coefficient (dimensionless), \text{CV}: coefficient of variation (dimensionless), \lambda_{\text{Browne}}: drawdown ruin penalty factor (dimensionless), \text{DD}_{\text{ruin}}: maximum tolerable drawdown threshold (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Outcomes follow a Beta-Binomial conjugate prior; higher-order moments are tractable via Cornish-Fisher expansion; drawdown dynamics approximate geometric Brownian motion for Browne's ruin approximation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities emerge when the posterior variance approaches zero (overconfidence) or when the CV penalty dominates expected edge, forcing f^* to negative values (shorting constraints violated).

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE risk-limiting order flow throttles; the Kelly fraction dictates the maximum allowable state transition velocity in the decision graph.
layer2.telemetry: Realized portfolio drawdown vs. theoretical Browne limit.

primitives.name: Copula Tail Dependence Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Copula tail dependence (Clayton, Gumbel, Frank, Gaussian, Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds, C-Vine simulation).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \lambda_U: upper tail dependence coefficient (dimensionless), u: marginal cumulative distribution function value (dimensionless), K(u,u): copula function evaluated at margins (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Marginal distributions are continuously distributed; dependence structure is stationary over the observation window; vine copulas satisfy the D-vine/C-vine recursive construction rules.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under regime shifts where historical tail dependence (e.g., Clayton lower tail) abruptly flips to upper tail clustering (Gumbel), violating the Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds used for stress testing.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI multivariate injury/roster impact modeling; C-Vines simulate cascading player unavailabilities affecting team strength priors.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical tail dependence ratio vs. fitted copula lambda.

primitives.name: Conformalized Count Prop Inference
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Poisson / Negative Binomial count props and CQR predictive intervals.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \hat{Q}_{\alpha}(x): conformalized quantile regression interval boundary (count units), \hat{F}^{-1}: inverse conditional CDF of Negative Binomial (count units), \hat{R}: nonconformity score residual (count units), \alpha: coverage level (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Exchangeability of calibration set residuals; underlying count data exhibits overdispersion adequately captured by Negative Binomial dispersion parameter; covariate shift is minimal.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Intervals become vacuous (spanning entire positive integers) if the calibration set lacks sufficient extreme event samples, causing the nonconformity score to diverge.

layer2.mapping: Directly feeds GSE ABSTAIN logic; if the CQR interval overlaps the sportsbook line entirely, the system enforces a hard veto on position sizing.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical coverage rate of observed counts within CQR bounds.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by establishing the Beta-Binomial posterior for binary outcomes, which serves as the foundational prior for the Bayesian Robust Kelly engine. Unlike classical Kelly, this operator integrates a Cornish-Fisher expansion to adjust the optimal fraction $f^*$ based on skewness and kurtosis, explicitly penalizing high coefficients of variation ($\kappa$). This penalty is further augmented by Browne's drawdown ruin probability, creating a highly conservative allocation strategy that naturally aligns with the fail-closed ABSTAIN enforcement mandated by Law 9. Concurrently, the Copula tail dependence operator models the joint distribution of extreme events across multiple assets or player metrics. By utilizing C-Vine simulations, we can accurately capture asymmetric dependencies (e.g., Clayton for lower tail clustering of injuries) that standard Gaussian assumptions miss. These multivariate extremes directly inform the Conditional Value-at-Risk limits applied to the Kelly fractions. Finally, the Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR) provides finite-sample valid predictive intervals for Poisson/Negative Binomial count props. The intersection of these three primitives forms a robust audit trail: the CQR intervals define the feasible action space, the Copula models the systemic risk of acting simultaneously on multiple props, and the Robust Kelly engine calculates the exact position size while guaranteeing that the probability of hitting a catastrophic drawdown remains below a predefined threshold. If the live feed connection drops or the negative control blocking triggers, the system instantly collapses all active Kelly fractions to zero, demonstrating a deterministic, mathematically sound fail-safe mechanism.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This lineage traces back to Kelly's 1956 logarithmic growth criterion, later refined by Thorp using card counting priors. The integration of Cornish-Fisher expansions echoes Edgeworth series developments in the early 20th century for approximating distribution functions. Browne's 1999 work on drawdown ruin introduced stochastic calculus boundaries to portfolio management. Modern conformal inference, pioneered by Vovk et al., brings rigorous frequentist guarantees to these Bayesian frameworks, completing the retrocausal loop from pure gambling theory to modern algorithmic risk management.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the opposing agent—the sportsbook or market maker—as a rational entity constantly adjusting lines to balance liability. Their 'mind' is represented by the shifting priors in our Beta-Binomial updates. When our CQR intervals detect a mispricing (an edge), we assume the market will eventually correct it, introducing a time-decay factor into our Kelly sizing. Furthermore, the Copula models the market's collective panic during tail events; if the market underestimates tail dependence (e.g., assuming independent player injuries), our C-Vine simulation reveals a hidden arbitrage opportunity that the market's simplified Gaussian mental model fails to price correctly.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by monitoring the correlation matrix derived from the Copula outputs. If the instantaneous correlation between two targeted props exceeds a critical threshold (approaching the Fréchet-Hoeffding upper bound), the system triggers a cross-layer veto, preventing simultaneous large allocations that would effectively double down on a single latent factor. Leakage is prevented by the strict separation between the calibration set (used for CQR) and the test set; any attempt to use future information to retroactively tighten intervals is caught by the deterministic re-run of `audit_tonight_snf.py`, which verifies that the output remains identical given the same historical seed, ensuring no temporal leakage corrupts the audit artifacts.
